extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A benchmark of 11.5K carefully selected multimodal college-level questions across 30 subjects and 183 subfields to evaluate multimodal understanding and reasoning with expert-level subject knowledge.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502v4 [cs.CL], 13 Jun 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was collected in three stages: selecting subjects based on common university majors and the presence of useful visual inputs; recruiting over 50 university students including co-authors to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and create new questions when necessary; then cleaning, formatting, and difficulty-filtering the collected questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Potential duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity and then reviewed by authors; problems were checked for format and typos; authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels and excluded about 10% classified as very easy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors and specializing in the selected majors, collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and created new questions when necessary. Annotators were instructed to follow copyright and license regulations and to prefer questions without immediately available answers to reduce contamination concerns.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors reviewed suspected duplicates, checked formatting and typos, and categorized problems into difficulty levels; approximately 10% of very easy problems were excluded.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in various majors and disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by the societal importance of monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled adult labor and lead to job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping to the 90th percentile of skilled adults and college exams are not the only tasks AGI should tackle; manual curation may carry biases; and the focus on college-level subjects may be insufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal models, including zero-shot evaluation, few-shot development, validation for hyperparameter selection, and test evaluation of expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning.

name.evidence: We introduce the Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning (MMMU) benchmark, a novel benchmark meticulously curated to assess the expert-level multimodal understanding capability of foundation models across a broad scope of tasks.

description.evidence: MMMU consists of 11.5K carefully selected multimodal questions, which cover 30 diverse subjects and 183 subfields, thus meeting the breadth goal.

inLanguage.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The live-updating leaderboard is available at: https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Data Collection. Our benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, we go through the common university majors to decide what subjects should be included in our benchmark. ... In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. ... Data Quality Control. To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. ... In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the arising data contamination concems of foundation models, the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.

Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: It denotes an AI system that reaches “at least 90th percentile of skilled adults” in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve “the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor” for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. ... MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MMMU, constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions.
